purpose: Whether a viewer can see what the window shows, judged by looking at it.
labelled_by: the assistant, from the three-frame strips the probe printed
honesty_note: These are not human labels. They were made by looking at each strip - which is the only way this question can be answered at all - but a person reviewing this file should re-check any label the floor turns on.

scale.WATCHABLE: a viewer can see what the food is and the shot is not distracting
scale.BORDERLINE: recognisable but abstract, or soft enough to be arguable
scale.UNWATCHABLE: blurred, blank, or otherwise unreadable as a picture of food

labels.label: UNWATCHABLE
labels.why: a blank grey frame; nothing in shot at all

labels.label: WATCHABLE
labels.why: a pin-sharp lime falling into water on a black background - sharp subject, empty surround

labels.label: BORDERLINE
labels.why: extreme macro of strawberry skin; the seeds read, the shot is abstract

labels.label: UNWATCHABLE
labels.why: a blurred hand squeezing a pale yellow object against blurred packaging; no apple a viewer could name

labels.label: WATCHABLE
labels.why: sharp avocado halves, clean studio background

labels.label: WATCHABLE
labels.why: sharp guacamole; the window spans a cut, which window_steadiness scores 0.030

finding: window_sharpness cannot carry a floor. It is mean edge density over the whole frame, so it measures how much of the frame is plain background rather than whether the subject is in focus. The set contains a pin-sharp lime at 0.000 and an unreadable blurred apple at 0.007: sharpness is not monotone in readability, and every floor that rejects the blur also rejects sharp subjects on plain backgrounds. window_centre_weight has the same fault for the same reason.
what_to_measure_instead: ANSWERED by run 34342326028, recorded in window_focus_metrics.json. laplacian_variance measured at 480x270 is the only candidate that both separates the labelled windows and rejects all three pexels:37239365 windows when the threshold is chosen without them. The same metric at 224x224 - what production decodes today - rejects none of them: the squash to the claim model's input lowpasses away the evidence blur leaves behind. Resolution is part of the answer, not an implementation detail.

candidate_threshold.aggregation: the weakest of the window's three sampled frames
candidate_threshold.how_chosen: geometric midpoint of the gap between the watchable minimum (39.48) and the highest non-held-out unwatchable window (4.81)
candidate_threshold.held_out_rejected: 3/3 - chosen without these and rejects them anyway
candidate_threshold.cost: 4 of the 45 windows that pass segment grounding, one of which is the known bad clip and one the BORDERLINE macro
candidate_threshold.not_shipped: Nothing gates on this. The low side of the gap rests on a single labelled window - a blank grey frame - and that is too thin an anchor to ship a production floor on.
